---
title: Coming from T3 Env or similar
description: Move a T3 Env (or similar) setup to zod-config's loadEnvConfig.
icon: ArrowRightLeft
---

`loadEnvConfig` keeps the shape of T3 Env's `createEnv`: `server` and `client` objects of Zod schemas, plus `runtimeEnv`.

| T3 Env | zod-config | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createEnv` from `@t3-oss/env-nextjs` | `loadEnvConfig` from `zod-config/nextjs` | Prefix fixed to `NEXT_PUBLIC_`. |
| `createEnv` from `@t3-oss/env-core` | `loadEnvConfig` from `zod-config` | Pass the prefix as `clientPrefix`. |
| `server`, `client`, `shared` | `server`, `client`, `shared` | Unchanged. |
| `runtimeEnv` | `runtimeEnv` | Works as it is. Server entries are optional (without them, server values come from `process.env`), but client entries must stay: client values are only read from `runtimeEnv`. |
| `runtimeEnvStrict` (env-core) | `runtimeEnv` with `strict: true` | Every server, client and shared key must be listed. |
| `onValidationError` | `onError` | Receives the Zod error rather than the issues array: use `error.issues`. Throw from it to replace the default error. |
| `skipValidation` | `skipValidation` | Returns raw values. Reading server variables in the browser still throws. |
| `import "./src/env"` in `next.config` | The same, or [`withZodConfigEnv`](/docs/env/nextjs#validate-when-nextjs-starts) | The wrapper also works with `next.config.mjs` and path aliases. On Vite, use the [`zodConfigEnv` plugin](/docs/env/vite#validate-when-vite-starts). |
| `isServer` | `isServer` | Unchanged. |

```ts twoslash title="src/env.ts"
import { loadEnvConfig } from 'zod-config/nextjs';
import { z } from 'zod';

export const env = loadEnvConfig({
  server: { DATABASE_URL: z.url() },
  client: { NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: z.url() },
  runtimeEnv: {
    DATABASE_URL: process.env.DATABASE_URL,
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL,
  },
  onError: (error) => {
    console.error(error.issues);
  },
});
```
